stories.headline: Delhi Cabinet clears plan to create ₹50-cr. corpus for start-ups
stories.title: Delhi Cabinet clears plan to create ₹50-cr. corpus for start-ups
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet clears' in title weight 44
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: The Delhi government has approved the setting up of the Go-Delhi Foundation, an initiative aimed at promoting startups, innovation and entrepreneurship in the capital.

The foundation will provide young people, researchers and entrepreneurs with integrated support to turn their ideas into practical products and successful enterprises, the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) said in a statement on Sunday.
It will have an initial budgetary outlay of ₹50 crore.
The Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, recently approved the foundation and sanctioned funds to help turn ideas into products and bring them to market.
Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the initiative is an important step towards bringing together Delhi’s existing entrepreneurial capabilities, educational institutions and research facilities.
“Delhi has nearly 21,000 start-ups recognised by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).

Through the Go-Delhi Foundation, these resources will be brought together on a common platform, with a focus on developing new enterprises, attracting investment and creating employment opportunities,” she said.
The foundation will help startups and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) access product engineering, prototyping, laboratory and testing facilities.
It will also offer mentorship and support entrepreneurs at different stages, from product development and testing to certification preparation and market access, Ms. Gupta said.
The foundation will be established as a not-for-profit company under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013, and function under the Delhi government’s Department of Industries.
Government departments will be able to bring their real-world challenges to Delhi’s innovators through the foundation, Ms. Gupta said.
Products and technologies developed to address these challenges could be tested through pilot projects, with successful solutions taken forward for adoption.

stories.headline: Supreme Court address a parental anxiety: How to keep the Internet safe for children | Explained
stories.title: Supreme Court address a parental anxiety: How to keep the Internet safe for children | Explained
stories.summary: Children cannot be blamed for CSEAM material online, the wrongdoer is the person who creates the content and the intermediary who slept on the watch
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The story so far: A Supreme Court judgment on October 15 addressed the everyday anxiety of parents, who are torn between allowing their children access to the Internet and the need to keep them safe from vile, abusive online content.

The judgment by a Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran reasons that the solution is not to ban children from using the Internet, but to take measures to keep them safe from exploitation by predators lurking online.
The court declared that a child, like any other individual, has a fundamental right to access and use the Internet.
The State, lawmakers and parents cannot blame children for the presence of Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM) on the Internet.
The wrongdoer is the person who creates, circulates, sells or seeks out such material, and the intermediary which fails to detect and remove the content.
To keep the child away from the Internet on account of such failures would be to mistake the victim for the problem.
Any measure for the safety of children must be directed at the harmful material and those responsible for the same, and not at the children themselves.
The court held that “our children are entitled to both safety and the freedom to access the Internet”.
To deny them the freedom to go online would be as absurd as saying children below a certain age did not have a conscience worth protecting or a freedom of speech worth expressing.

The court found that its directions for online child safety in a September 23, 2024 judgment in a petition filed by Justice Rights for Children Alliance were largely ignored for the past two years, leading to serious lapses.
The court said there had been an “alarming increase” in child sexual exploitation and CSEAM circulated on social media platforms.

It flagged how indirect links to such harmful material were promoted and shared through social media algorithms to bypass the rigours of the special penal provisions designed for the protection of children within cyberspace.

stories.headline: Kashmir University orders stock verification of library books
stories.title: Kashmir University orders stock verification of library books
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 18: Authorities at Kashmir University (KU) have directed all departments, research centres, campuses and directorates to undertake physical verification of library books and submit verified reports within two months. As per the fresh circular instructions, the departments and research centres have been asked to focus on scrutiny of missing books and losses involving high-value titles. The circular instructions in this regard have been issued by Librarian of the Allama Iqbal Library of the varsity on October 16, 2026. The KU Librarian has asked Heads of Departments (HoDs) and Directors of various research centres, directorates and campuses to immediately initiate the stock-verification exercise to ensure accountability, proper maintenance and accurate updating of library assets. The concerned departments and centres have been asked to constitute internal stock-verification committees and submit final reports along with the prescribed annexures to the University Librarian's office within the stipulated period. The exercise will cover total library holdings, books currently available, weeded-out titles, books damaged in the 2014 floods, losses reported by users, books in circulation and records of books issued or consulted between January 2001 and December 2025. The University has also directed departments to calculate missing-book losses in accordance with the General Financial Rules (GFR) 2017, particularly Rule 215, read with the University Library Committee's resolutions. Under the prescribed procedure, institutions will have to reconcile missing-book figures with circulation records to establish whether the losses fall within the permissible limits. As per the circular instructions, the HoDs and Directors have been asked to submit detailed written explanations in cases where a missing book has a purchase cost exceeding Rs 1,000. The instructions have been issued along with the amendments to the University's stock-verification regulations approved by the Library Committee, which provide that the loss of five books per 1,000 volumes issued or consulted annually may be considered reasonable, provided the losses are not attributable to dishonesty or negligence. The amended provision, according to the committee's minutes dated January 23, 2025, is to be applied retrospectively. The committee has also clarified that books consulted within library premises for reading, reference or study, as well as those taken off shelves for photocopying without formal issuance, will be counted as consulted books while calculating allowable losses. For the purpose of estimating consultations, the committee has prescribed figures of three books for students, five each for scholars and faculty members, and one book for staff and other officials. The University has prescribed separate formats for stock verification and the preparation of missing-book lists. In view of this, all the departments will have to provide details such as accession numbers, titles, authors and printed prices of missing books, with the total cost to be calculated by Allama Iqbal Library. "The missing-book lists must be prepared in MS Excel and sent through the official email ID of the concerned Head of Department to the designated library email addresses," the circular reads.
